statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail risk sits in the watch band while cross-asset stress remains high ahead of the September payrolls release.
recommendation: Tail at 20% remains below the block threshold, so the mapped state stays WATCH. The elevated component of this assessment is concentrated in the narrow 12:30-14:00 UTC payrolls window on 2 October rather than in any observed overnight price structure.
headline: Nasdaq-100 mean-reverts into the close as yields retreat from 2002 highs; September payrolls is the next checkpoint
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,501.56, up 0.31%, after rejecting a 30,274.65 session low and recovering roughly two thirds of the intraday decline. Long-dated yields drove the early weakness, with the 10-year reaching 5.33%, its highest since early 2002, before easing to 5.24%; the 2-year fell about 11 basis points to 4.80% as October rate-hike odds dropped to 34% from 70% a week earlier. Micron's earnings beat and raised guidance lifted the semiconductor complex and carried into Asia. Against that, Brent crude jumped above $100 and WTI settled near $92 after reports of a third U.S. carrier strike group heading to the Middle East, and the ISM manufacturing prices-paid index surged to 77.9. NQ futures are holding a narrow band near 30,850 overnight. The observed price path is two-sided rather than one-way: retracements occurred in both directions and the VIX decayed from 17.59 to 16.39, which keeps Tail inside the watch band. Stress is high because yields near multidecade peaks, an energy-led inflation channel and an unresolved Gulf escalation track coincide with a Tier-1 labour-market print.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry published Claude assessments. Tail held a 20-25 range with a single 25 print at 06:00 UTC during the European pre-market, and Stress climbed from 70 to a 78 peak around the 14:00 UTC ISM manufacturing release before easing to 74 into the close. Dominant mode was mixed throughout apart from two trend-up prints in the European morning.
outlookSummary: The overnight Asian and European hours carry no scheduled U.S. catalyst, so Tail is held in the 20-23 watch band with Stress drifting up as the payrolls countdown shortens. Tail steps to 25 for exactly the two hours covering the 12:30 UTC release and the 13:30 UTC cash open, where a hot wage print into a 5.24% 10-year is a credible yield-led no-retracement mechanism, then eases back on the assumption of orderly two-way price discovery. Equity index futures close for the weekend at 20:00 UTC on 2 October, after which the residual exposure is weekend gap and Gulf headline risk rather than an intraday path.
